lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Yolanda, this is Yolanda. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're dealing with a lot, and you still made time for this call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the soda swap?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Only 2 days. We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Family time comes first, and food is a big part of that.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I need this for my head too, not just my body. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I just didn't feel like it. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You just weren't feeling it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the parties makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you keep soda in the house?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I know I can do it, I did it before. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe swap soda for water on 5 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 5.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 5 and not a 2?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 2 out of 4 days, the hard part was the parties, and next week you're going to swap soda for water on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Yolanda, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: No help from daughter; family event
Sides with barrier; may reinforce sustain talk
Feels better about self when sticking to it

flags.reason: Participant said she is 'kind of down this week'; coach did not explore mood and moved to soda goal. Consider checking mood or screening for depression.
Repeats the identical seltzer-with-lime suggestion from line 12 without new permission or tailoring after participant already responded to it.
Coach affirmed the family barrier ('Family time comes first') instead of reflecting the participant's desire to change, reinforcing sustain talk.

score.summary: The coach built useful momentum by eliciting change talk, asking the participant to propose her own goal (5 days of water), and planning for barriers and a summary. However, the coach skipped exploring the participant's low mood and repeated the same seltzer suggestion verbatim, which reduced partnership.
strengths: Line 22 and line 14: affirmed effort and the starting step, supporting self-efficacy.
Line 49: 'It's completely your call' emphasized autonomy around the new goal.
Line 52: 'Why a 5 and not a 2?' drew out confidence reasons.
Line 56: summary recapped barriers and plan before closing.
coaching_tips: Line 4: when she says she is 'kind of down,' pause and ask an open question about her mood before returning to the goal.
Line 45: rather than repeating the seltzer tip, ask permission and tailor it to her party and church barriers.
Line 18: reflect her desire ('you want to feel like yourself again', line 13) instead of agreeing with the family-barrier framing.
Line 6 and 28: good open questions; keep building on her own plans such as the fridge reminder (line 42).
